name: M-2 long bridge, probable Jhelum River crossing near Bhera
assumptions: No photograph of this bridge from the side, from below or from the deck could be found. Only satellite imagery shows it; the road photos are of other parts of the M-2.
River identity is unconfirmed by name: Esri imagery shows a large river under the bridge, and the dossier infers the Jhelum from geography.
Deck level 10.0 m at the south-east end and 11.1 m at the north-west end, read from approach embankments at 196.0 and 197.1 m on z15 terrain, against 186.0 m at the origin; no survey.

Deck width 13.6 m, gap under 1 m, 9.6 m dark surface and 2 m pale edge bands measured on Esri at about 0.5 m per pixel. That surface is narrower than three standard lanes would need, and the true split may differ.
Span count 18 (45.4 m spans) is a guess; no source gives it and the deck hides the piers in the imagery.
Single-cell concrete box girder of constant 3.0 m depth is inferred from Structurae's note of incremental launching for a 'Bhaira bridge', which is not confirmed to be this bridge.

One chamfered wall pier 6.0 by 1.8 m under each deck is the plainest plausible form; the pier type is unknown. Foundations and footings are not modelled, and piers run 2.5 m below the origin to cover terrain differences.
Barrier profile (1.0 m concrete safety barrier on both edges of each deck) is taken from other M-2 road photos; the barrier positions match the pale edge bands on Esri.
Colours: road surfaces sampled from Esri, barrier hue from M-2 road photos, girder and pier greys estimated.
Yellow edge lines come from M-2 road photos of other sections. Two dashed lane lines per deck are visible on Esri; the 6 m dash and 12 m gap are estimated.
Abutments are plain walls with 9.5 m of fill behind them on 1 in 1.25 slopes; the real wing walls and embankment slopes are unknown, and the approach road is left to the game.
No lamp columns, signs or expansion joints are modelled because none can be seen on Esri at this resolution.
suppress is empty on purpose: the dossier footprint is only a centreline, and flattening a strip of river bed and banks under it is not wanted.
No night lighting: no source describes any.
